title: A Zoo of Fermionic Relative Rényi Negativities in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Models
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource that gives rise to correlations with no classical counterpart in strongly correlated fermionic systems. However, its characterization in mixed quantum states remains challenging. Established entanglement diagnostics, such as logarithmic negativity, are computationally demanding in interacting systems, and their evaluation by exact diagonalization is restricted to small system sizes. Meanwhile, conventional Rényi proxies, including twisted and untwisted Rényi negativities, can be positive even for separable states. In this work, we introduce a family of \textit{relative Rényi negativities} that serve as entanglement witnesses. By relating fermionic partial time reversal to the size superoperator, we establish a path-integral representation for these Rényi negativities, enabling their evaluation in thermal states of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and its generalizations via a large-$N$ expansion. Applying this method, we investigate entanglement in both the original SYK model and the Maldacena-Qi coupled SYK model. We identify a special class of relative Rényi negativities which serve as plausible proxies for logarithmic negativity and uncover first-order entanglement transitions that are invisible to simple observables. These results highlight the utility of relative Rényi negativities as probes of mixed-state entanglement in strongly correlated fermionic systems and suggest the existence of a new class of transitions where these negativities serve as free energies.
summary: This paper introduces a novel family of relative Rényi negativities to diagnose entanglement in mixed quantum states of strongly correlated fermionic systems. By deriving a path-integral representation applicable to the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model, the authors provide a computationally feasible method. This work reveals new entanglement signatures, including first-order transitions, that are otherwise hidden from simple measurements.
main_problem: The primary challenge is characterizing quantum entanglement in mixed quantum states, as established diagnostics are computationally demanding or restricted to small systems.
main_result: The authors introduce relative Rényi negativities as entanglement witnesses, successfully identifying a class that proxies logarithmic negativity and revealing first-order entanglement transitions invisible to simpler observables.
method: They derive a path-integral representation for these negativities by relating fermionic partial time reversal to the size superoperator, enabling evaluation via a large-N expansion.
model_or_system: The study focuses on strongly correlated fermionic systems, specifically the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and its generalizations, including the Maldacena-Qi coupled SYK model.
key_observables: Relative Rényi negativities ($P_f^A$), Logarithmic Negativity, and entanglement entropy.
important_parameters: Large-$N$ limit, thermal states, and the structure of the fermionic interactions (random $q$-body couplings).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the path-integral formalism and the large-$N$ expansion, noting that conventional Rényi proxies can fail to certify entanglement.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of relative Rényi negativities, derives their path-integral representation, and applies this method to calculate entanglement measures in the SYK model, culminating in the identification of new transition types.
why_interesting: The development of new, tractable entanglement witnesses that work for mixed states in strongly interacting fermionic models provides powerful tools for understanding quantum correlations beyond simple ground-state calculations.
